issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for Animal and its subclasses: the solution code defines a two-parameter constructor (Animal(String name, int age)) and subclasses (e.g. Seal(String name, int age)), while the problem statement and the template Main example instantiate animals using a single String argument (e.g. new Seal("Clarabelle")). This mismatch will cause compilation errors or confusion when students use the provided Main example or follow the problem text.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor API consistent across artifacts. Preferred (backwards-compatible) fix: add single-argument constructors that accept only String name in Animal and in each subclass that delegate to the existing two-argument constructors (e.g. public Animal(String name) { this(name, /*defaultAge*/0); } and corresponding subclass ctors). Alternative: update the problem statement and the template Main example to require and demonstrate two-argument constructors (String name, int age) and document the additional age attribute.

issues.description: The solution's Animal class introduces an additional attribute 'age' (private int age) which is not present in the UML and problem specification (the UML and text specify only a 'name: String' attribute for Animal). This extra attribute changes the required constructor signature and the class API compared to the problem statement/template and may confuse students about the expected model.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Animal attributes with the specification. Options: (A) Remove the 'age' field and its getters/setters from the solution so Animal only has 'name', and provide single-argument constructors; or (B) Update the problem statement and template to explicitly include an 'age' attribute (document its type and constructor usage) and update the examples. If keeping 'age' in the solution, add single-argument constructors (with a sensible default age) to preserve compatibility with the existing template examples.
